subject: Future Tech
title: Grey Goo: Real Threat or Myth?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Grey Goo: Real Threat or Myth?.

hook.text: Self-replicating nanobots consume all matter on Earth to make copies of themselves.

buildup.text: Drexler described grey goo as a theoretical risk: molecular assemblers replicating without limits, consuming everything.

twist.text: Real nano-risks are mundane: workplace exposure, environmental contamination, and weapons development.

climax.text: The myth persists in pop culture but no credible scientist considers it a near-term risk.

punchline.text: The scariest nano-scenario is fiction. The real risks are boring and urgent.

quiz.question: Why do scientists not consider grey goo a credible near-term threat?
options: Self-replicating nanobots need capabilities far beyond current science
